Description

CB1 is the neuronal cannabinoid receptor, found on nociceptors and on their central terminals in the dorsal horn. Endocannabinoids activate it on demand, and Gi then inhibits adenylate cyclase while Gβγ closes calcium channels and reduces transmitter release. In rodent OA, raising endocannabinoid levels reduces joint afferent firing and pain through CB1.

Colour

Each block is coloured by its effect on pain, red where it raises pain and blue where it relieves it, and everything in it takes that colour, GTP and GDP included, as it works for the block's result. Drugs are yellow and classes of molecules white.

This block is blue: CB1 inhibits the release of transmitters.
